newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares trade firmer but seen weak again.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares trade firmer but seen weak again.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index gained some points on Tuesday but brokers said this was only a temporary recovery with fundamentals still pointing to a general weakness for the next two month or so.

"I don't see it (gain) being anything other than temporary. Interest rates are trending upwards, especially with the latest rediscount rate, so we're expecting apathy in the stock market to continue," commented one broker.
She said the market was likely to take direction only after the government's annual budget announcement in July.
"It will depend on whether there's any good news in the budget and what policies are put in place for the next year in the budget commentary," she said.

On Tuesday, the main industrial index added 41.65 points to 10,056.97, buoyed by advances in bankers FMB and NMB, both 100 cents firmer at 4,300 and 3,200 respectively, while another banking house, Barclays put on 75 cents to 2,900.
Timber producers Border went up 50 cents to 1,500, tyre firm NTS put on 40 cents to 350 and regional multi-industrial giant TZI TZI.ZI gained 20 cents to 1,040.
Minings remained lifeless as international gold prices continued weak. The seven share mining index lost 5.09 points to 957.31.
